instruction: Load environment variables from a file.
Load multiple environment files, with later ones overriding earlier.
Set inline environment variables in the unit.
Make an environment file optional so the unit starts even if it is missing.
Pass a variable into a shell command inside ExecStart.
Reference another unit's environment via a drop-in.
Use a secrets file with restricted permissions.
output:
[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/etc/myapp/secrets.env
# chmod 600 /etc/myapp/secrets.env, owned by root
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/app

instruction: Quote values containing spaces in an environment file.
output:
# /etc/myapp/env (no export, no quotes needed unless spaces)
APP_NAME=My Application
APP_TAG="release candidate"
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/app

instruction: Explain the format of EnvironmentFile and common mistakes.
output:
# Files use KEY=VALUE, one per line. Do NOT use 'export'.
# Quotes are optional but required for values with spaces.
# Comments start with #. Line continuations use a trailing backslash.
[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/etc/myapp/env

instruction: Set a service-specific PATH via EnvironmentFile.
Override an environment variable with an ExecStart prefix.
Expand a variable inside another variable in the unit.
Load environment from a file and ensure it is only readable by root.
Use LoadCredential to inject a secret as a file.
Set locale-related environment variables.
Undefine a variable for a single command.
Use an EnvironmentFile with systemd specifiers.
Demonstrate the precedence of environment sources.
output:
[Service]
# Precedence (low to high): EnvironmentFile=, Environment=, inline in ExecStart
EnvironmentFile=/etc/myapp/env
Environment=LOG_LEVEL=debug
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env LOG_LEVEL=trace /usr/local/bin/app

instruction: Set a default value using an environment file plus inline fallback.
Comment the pitfalls of spaces around '=' in env files.
output:
# WRONG: KEY = value (spaces become part of the key/value)
# RIGHT: KEY=value
